title: LIC's September-quarter profit rises 20% to Rs 12,076 crore; first-year premiums slip
dek: Net premium income grows 16% on single-premium policies, but new regular-premium business falls 3.7% and LIC's market share edges down.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC), the country's largest insurer, said its net profit for the July-September quarter rose 20% from a year earlier to Rs 12,076 crore, helped by a 16% rise in net premium income. Its board approved the results on Thursday.

The profit compares with Rs 10,053 crore in the same quarter last year, according to Business Standard and Indian PSU. It was, however, about 10% lower than the Rs 13,492 crore LIC earned in the April-June quarter, according to Lapaas Voice. Total income for the quarter was Rs 2,62,739 crore.

## Premiums: single policies up, first-year sales down

Net premium income rose 16.2% to Rs 1,47,018 crore. The growth came mostly from single-premium policies, where the customer pays once, which rose about 35%. Renewal premiums from existing policyholders rose 5.2% to Rs 68,375 crore.

First-year premium income, which measures new regular-premium business and is closely watched as a sign of future growth, fell 3.7% to Rs 10,432 crore, Indian PSU reported. LIC's share of first-year premium across the life insurance industry slipped to 58.77% from 59.41% a year earlier, according to The Hindu BusinessLine as summarised by Indian Opinion.

The gross non-performing assets ratio on LIC's loan book fell to 1.16% from 1.21% in the previous quarter, Indian PSU reported.

## Profitability of new business

The value of new business (VNB), which estimates the future profit from policies sold in the period, rose about 34% to Rs 6,846 crore for the April-September half, and the VNB margin widened to 22.3% from 17.6% a year earlier, according to the reports. A higher margin means LIC is selling a more profitable mix of products, such as non-participating policies, on which it keeps more of the profit than on traditional "with-profit" policies.

For the first half of the financial year, standalone net profit was Rs 25,568 crore, up 21.5%, according to Lapaas Voice, which also reported a solvency ratio of 2.35 against 2.13 a year earlier and assets under management of Rs 59.61 lakh crore. It also reported that LIC sold 70.97 lakh individual policies in the half, 2.25% fewer than a year earlier, and that its expense ratio fell to 10.41% from 11.28%.

## Background

LIC is majority-owned by the Union government. Its results matter well beyond its own shareholders: it is one of the largest investors in Indian shares and government bonds, so its premium flows feed directly into the country's financial markets.

Private insurers have been gaining ground in new business for several years, which is why analysts track LIC's first-year premium and market share closely.

Lapaas Voice reported that LIC has received regulatory approval to defer its move to the Ind AS accounting standards by a year, to 1 April 2027.

## What happens next

LIC's shares, which fell 7.3% in October according to Goodreturns, will trade on the results for the first time when markets open on Friday. The Declaration could not access LIC's own results filing before publication; the figures above are taken from news reports of the results, and the half-year, solvency and assets figures come from a single report.
